docs.title: Ryu
docs.text:
"Nothing ever works on the first compile. That's what makes the second one feel like a power-up arc."

Ryu is a set of C++/QML components for Qt 6, built because the existing ones were either ugly or didn't exist. Material 3 styling, springy animations, and widgets that have seen things.

It is a personal project. It works on my machine. Your machine is a side quest.

docs.title: What's inside
docs.text:
Module What it does Docs Extraa Material 3 widgets: WavyProgress, MaterialSlider, MaterialIconButton, MaterialButtonGroup Partly Shapes MaterialShape, with 35 shapes that morph into each other using springs Yes Cleave Audio visualizer. PipeWire in, FFT out, bars go brrr Soon™ Clipsh Clipboard history on top of cliphist and wl-copy Soon™ Sqliter SQLite-backed events storage Soon™ Warsa Nepali (BS) calendar logic Soon™

"Soon™" means the code exists and the documentation is still in its training arc.

docs.title: Arch Linux (AUR)
docs.text:
Ryu is on the AUR in two flavors. Pick one, because they conflict with each other.

ryu-bin (prebuilt)ryu (from source)

Installs the release binaries. Fast, no compiler needed.

paru -S ryu-bin

Builds from the tagged release with CMake and Ninja. Slower, but compiled against your own Qt.

paru -S ryu

Any AUR helper works (yay -S ryu-bin). To install by hand:

git clone https://aur.archlinux.org/ryu-bin.git
cd ryu-bin
makepkg -si

Dependencies (qt6-base, qt6-declarative, cliphist, wl-clipboard, pipewire) are pulled in automatically. The modules are installed to /usr/lib/qt6/qml/Ryu/, so they work with any Qt 6 QML app or Quickshell config, no extra import paths needed:

import Ryu.Extraa
import Ryu.Shapes

Module not installed?

If you see module "Ryu.Extraa" is not installed, the package isn't installed yet. makepkg only builds it, so run makepkg -si (or sudo pacman -U on the built package) and try again.

docs.title: Other distros
docs.text: No packages yet. Build from source and install with ninja -C build install, or embed Ryu in your app as a submodule.

docs.title: Build from source
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/Happilli/ryu
cd ryu
./build.sh            # configure + build with CMake and Ninja
./build.sh --clean    # burn the build directory and start over

Then, in QML:

import Ryu.Extraa

MaterialSlider {
    width: 240
    value: 0.5
    onMoved: console.log(value)
}

To try a file without an app around it, point the qml tool at the build directory:

qml -I build test.qml

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
You'll need:

  • Qt 6 with Quick and Sql
  • CMake and Ninja
  • A font with the icons you want (a Nerd Font or Material Symbols), because icon glyphs without one are just tofu and regret

And, depending on what you use:

  • PipeWire for Cleave
  • cliphist and wl-clipboard for Clipsh (Wayland only)
  • Python with requests and beautifulsoup4 for the Warsa month-length scraper

On Arch, the AUR packages handle all of this for you.

docs.title: A note on colors
docs.text:
Every Extraa component defaults to the classic M3 purple. Set your own colors, or enjoy purple forever:

MaterialSlider {
    color: "#a0ec4c"
    handleColor: "#a0ec4c"
    trackColor: "#32362b"
}

docs.title: Known quirks
docs.text:
Things that will bite you

  • WavyProgress animates by default (indeterminate: true). A bare one spins forever, like a deadline.
  • Changing MaterialSlider.orientation swaps width and height. Set the size in Component.onCompleted if they start fighting.
  • Icon glyphs need iconFont set, or you get empty boxes.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Found a bug? Open an issue. Fixed one? Open a PR. Both are welcome, and neither will be judged harshly, only silently.

docs.title: License
docs.text: BSD 2-Clause. Do what you want, keep the notice, and don't blame me when it breaks.

docs.title: Embedding Ryu
docs.text:
Besides installing Ryu system-wide, you can build it into your own app as a git submodule. The modules are compiled statically and linked straight into your executable, so users don't need Ryu installed.

This is how typeShi uses it.

docs.title: When to embed
docs.text: Installed (AUR) Embedded (submodule) Users need Ryu installed Yes No Ryu version Whatever is installed Pinned by your repo Works for Quickshell configs, qml scripts Standalone Qt 6 apps Rebuild on Ryu update No Yes

docs.title: 1. Add the submodule
docs.text:
git submodule add https://github.com/Happilli/ryu third_party/ryu
git commit -m "add ryu"

Your repo records the exact Ryu commit, so upstream changes never reach you until you update the submodule yourself.

docs.title: 2. CMake
docs.text:
Set the options before add_subdirectory, then link the targets.

find_package(Qt6 REQUIRED COMPONENTS Core Gui Qml Quick)

set(RYU_MODULES "Shapes" CACHE STRING "" FORCE)
set(RYU_STATIC  ON       CACHE BOOL   "" FORCE)
set(RYU_INSTALL OFF      CACHE BOOL   "" FORCE)
add_subdirectory(third_party/ryu)

qt_add_executable(myapp main.cpp)

target_link_libraries(myapp PRIVATE
    Qt6::Core Qt6::Gui Qt6::Qml Qt6::Quick
    Ryu::Shapes
    Ryu::Shapesplugin
)

qt_import_qml_plugins(myapp)
  • RYU_MODULES is a semicolon-separated list. Build only what you use. Valid names: Cleave, Clipsh, Sqliter, Warsa, Shapes, Extraa, Widgets. An unknown name stops the configure with Unknown Ryu module.
  • RYU_STATIC / RYU_INSTALL: when Ryu is added as a subdirectory, these already default to ON / OFF. The example sets them anyway so the intent is visible. When Ryu is the top-level project the defaults are reversed.
  • Targets: each module Name gives you two aliases, Ryu::Name and Ryu::Nameplugin. Link both. Without the plugin target the QML types are not registered.
  • qt_import_qml_plugins is required for static builds. It pulls the plugins your QML imports into the executable.
  • Several modules: set(RYU_MODULES "Shapes;Extraa" CACHE STRING "" FORCE) and link Ryu::Extraa and Ryu::Extraaplugin as well.

Extraa, Shapes and Widgets depend on an internal RyuCore library. It is built and linked for you.

docs.title: 3. Use it in QML
docs.text:
Import the module by name, exactly as with the installed version:

import QtQuick
import Ryu.Shapes

MaterialShape {
    width: 96
    height: 96
    shape: MaterialShape.Cookie7Sided
}

Nothing else is needed in main.cpp.

docs.title: Module requirements
docs.text:
Module Extra dependency Shapes, Extraa, Widgets, Warsa, Clipsh None beyond Qt Quick Sqliter Qt6::Sql (added for you) Cleave pipewire (found with pkg-config; configure fails if it is missing) Clipsh (at runtime) cliphist and wl-clipboard

Only the modules listed in RYU_MODULES are checked, so leaving out Cleave means no PipeWire needed to build.

docs.title: Packaging an embedded app
docs.text:
Source tarballs do not contain submodules

Archives that GitHub or Gitea generate for a tag (.../archive/refs/tags/v1.0.tar.gz) leave third_party/ryu as an empty directory. A build from such a tarball fails with:

The source directory .../third_party/ryu does not contain a CMakeLists.txt file.

Pick one of these fixes.

docs.title: Option A: git+ source (PKGBUILD)
docs.text:
makedepends=('git' 'cmake' 'ninja')
source=("$pkgname::git+https://github.com/you/myapp.git#tag=v$pkgver")
sha256sums=('SKIP')

prepare() {
  cd "$srcdir/$pkgname"
  git submodule update --init --recursive
}

SKIP is expected for git+ sources. The pinned tag (or #commit=) is the integrity check, and the submodule commit is recorded in your repo.

docs.title: Option B: tarball plus a pinned Ryu tarball
docs.text:
Use this if you want real checksums for everything.

_ryu_commit=<the commit your submodule points at>
source=("$pkgname-$pkgver.tar.gz::https://github.com/you/myapp/archive/refs/tags/v$pkgver.tar.gz"
        "ryu-$_ryu_commit.tar.gz::https://github.com/Happilli/ryu/archive/$_ryu_commit.tar.gz")
sha256sums=('...' '...')   # updpkgsums fills these in

prepare() {
  cp -a "$srcdir/ryu-$_ryu_commit/." "$srcdir/myapp-$pkgver/third_party/ryu/"
}

Find the commit with git ls-tree v1.0 third_party/ryu (look for mode 160000). Whenever you bump the submodule, change _ryu_commit and re-run updpkgsums.

docs.title: CI
docs.text:
With GitHub Actions, check out the submodule:

- uses: actions/checkout@v5
  with:
    submodules: recursive

docs.title: Updating Ryu
docs.text:
git -C third_party/ryu fetch
git -C third_party/ryu checkout <new-commit>
git add third_party/ryu
git commit -m "update ryu"

If you package with Option B, update _ryu_commit to match.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause and fix does not contain a CMakeLists.txt file Submodule not fetched. Run git submodule update --init --recursive, or see Packaging. Unknown Ryu module: X Typo in RYU_MODULES. Names are case-sensitive. module "Ryu.Shapes" is not installed at runtime The plugin target is missing from target_link_libraries, or qt_import_qml_plugins was not called. plugin 'Shapesplugin' ... does not exist in the current scope The module was not built. Check that it is listed in RYU_MODULES before add_subdirectory. qmldir file not found at .../build/<YourModule> A harmless message when your own QML module is built with NO_PLUGIN. It is not related to Ryu. Could NOT find WrapVulkanHeaders Optional Qt dependency. Ignore it.

docs.title: Cleave
docs.text:
An audio visualizer backend. Cleave listens to your system audio through PipeWire, runs an FFT on it, and hands QML a list of frequency band levels. It draws nothing itself. You decide whether the bands become bars, a ring, a blob, or something worse.

This one is a string pinned at both ends that vibrates with the music, with the bass in the middle and the treble toward the edges. Its color comes from the system palette, so it follows light and dark mode automatically.

import QtQuick
import Ryu.Cleave

Item {
    id: root
    width: 480
    height: 160

    property color stringColor: palette.windowText

    Cleave {
        id: cleave
        bandCount: 24
        smoothing: 0.85
        Component.onCompleted: startCapture()
        onDataChanged: canvas.requestPaint()
        onError: msg => console.warn("Cleave:", msg)
    }

    onStringColorChanged: canvas.requestPaint()

    Canvas {
        id: canvas
        anchors.fill: parent
        antialiasing: true

        onPaint: {
            const ctx = getContext("2d")
            ctx.clearRect(0, 0, width, height)

            const m = cleave.magnitudes
            const n = m.length
            if (n === 0)
                return

            const midY = height / 2
            const maxAmp = height * 0.4
            const pad = 12
            const w = width - pad * 2
            const count = n * 2

            const pts = []
            for (let i = 0; i < count; ++i) {
                const t = i / (count - 1)
                const k = i < n ? n - 1 - i : i - n
                const level = Math.min(1, m[k] * 5)
                const pin = Math.sin(t * Math.PI)
                const dir = (i % 2 === 0) ? 1 : -1

                pts.push({
                    x: pad + t * w,
                    y: midY + dir * level * maxAmp * pin
                })
            }

            ctx.lineWidth = 2.5
            ctx.lineCap = "round"
            ctx.lineJoin = "round"
            ctx.strokeStyle = root.stringColor

            ctx.beginPath()
            ctx.moveTo(pts[0].x, pts[0].y)
            for (let i = 1; i < pts.length - 1; ++i) {
                const mx = (pts[i].x + pts[i + 1].x) / 2
                const my = (pts[i].y + pts[i + 1].y) / 2
                ctx.quadraticCurveTo(pts[i].x, pts[i].y, mx, my)
            }
            const last = pts[pts.length - 1]
            ctx.lineTo(last.x, last.y)
            ctx.stroke()
        }
    }
}

How it works:

  • Theme: palette.windowText is dark in light mode and light in dark mode, so the line is always readable. Use palette.highlight for an accent color, or a fixed color if you prefer.
  • Pinned ends: the sin(t * π) taper flattens the line at both ends, like a real string.
  • Mirroring: the spectrum is reflected around the center so the curve is symmetric and has no seam.
  • Tuning: change the * 5 gain and maxAmp to taste, and raise smoothing toward 0.9 for a calmer line.
  • Repaint on theme change: the onStringColorChanged handler redraws the canvas, otherwise the old color would stay until the next audio update.

Cleave does not start by itself

Nothing happens until you call startCapture(). The example does it in Component.onCompleted.

docs.title: Analysis
docs.text: Property Type Default Description bandCount int 32 Number of frequency bands, clamped to 2 to 512. Changing it resets all levels to zero. smoothing real 0.75 How much of the previous level is kept each frame, clamped to 0 to 0.99. Higher is smoother and slower. 0 is raw. peakDecay real 0.02 How much the peak markers fall per frame, clamped to 0.001 to 0.5. Also the speed at which the levels fall to zero after the sound stops. silenceThreshold real 0.0001 Frames quieter than this (RMS of the samples, 0 to 1) are ignored. source string empty What to capture. Empty means the default audio output (what you hear). See Choosing a source. debugMode bool false Prints capture state and a once-a-second status line to the console.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Property Type Description magnitudes list<real> Current level of each band, lowest frequency first. Its length is bandCount. peaks list<real> Slowly falling peak of each band, the same length as magnitudes. fps int How many FFT frames were processed in the last second. This is the analysis rate, not your screen's frame rate.

docs.title: State
docs.text: Property Type Description active bool Read-only. True while a capture stream is running. suspended bool Read-only. True after Cleave stopped itself because the audio went quiet. See Auto-suspend.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text: Method Description startCapture() Connects to PipeWire and starts analysing. Returns true on success. On failure it returns false and emits error. Calling it again restarts the stream. stopCapture() Stops the stream and clears the buffers. active and suspended both become false. resumeCapture() Restarts the capture and emits suspendedChanged if it had been suspended. Use this to wake Cleave up after an auto-suspend. reset() Zeroes all levels and clears the pending audio, without touching the stream.

docs.title: Signals
docs.text:
Signal Description dataChanged() New levels are available. Emitted for magnitudes, peaks and fps. activeChanged() active changed. suspendedChanged() suspended changed. error(string msg) Something failed: creating the PipeWire loop or stream, connecting, or a stream error while running.

The other ...Changed signals (bandCountChanged, smoothingChanged, peakDecayChanged, silenceThresholdChanged, sourceChanged, debugModeChanged) work as usual.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Cleave asks PipeWire for a mono, 32-bit float stream at 48 kHz.
  • Audio is cut into windows of 2048 samples, shaped with a Hann window and run through an FFT. Windows overlap by half, so you get up to about 47 updates per second.
  • The bands are spaced logarithmically from about 70 Hz to about 16 kHz, so the bass gets as much room as the treble. Higher bands are boosted slightly to even out the natural tilt of music.
  • Each band is smoothed with smoothing and tracked with a falling peak.

The first few bands are the bass, which is what makes a kick drum thump.

docs.title: Choosing a source
docs.text:
By default Cleave captures the default output, so it reacts to whatever you are playing. To pick something else, set source:

Cleave {
    source: "alsa_output.pci-0000_00_1f.3.analog-stereo.monitor"
}
  • A name ending in .monitor means "capture what this output is playing".
  • Any other name targets that node directly, for example a microphone.

To find the names on your system, run pactl list short sources or pw-cli ls Node.

docs.title: Auto-suspend
docs.text:
To avoid burning CPU on silence, Cleave stops itself after the sound has been quiet for 3 seconds:

  1. The sound stops. The levels fall to zero at the rate set by peakDecay.
  2. After 3 seconds the stream is closed, active becomes false and suspended becomes true.
  3. Nothing wakes it up automatically. You have to call resumeCapture() when audio comes back.

The usual way is to listen for your player's playing state:

Cleave {
    id: cleave
    Component.onCompleted: startCapture()
}

Connections {
    target: player

    function onPlayingChanged() {
        if (player.playing && cleave.suspended)
            cleave.resumeCapture()
    }
}

Here player is whatever you already use to know that music is playing, such as an MPRIS player.

docs.title: Handling errors
docs.text:
startCapture() returns false when it fails, and error carries the reason. This also covers stream errors that happen while running.

Cleave {
    onError: msg => console.warn("Cleave:", msg)
    Component.onCompleted: {
        if (!startCapture())
            console.warn("could not start capture")
    }
}

docs.title: Calmer, slower response
docs.text:
Cleave {
    smoothing: 0.9
    peakDecay: 0.005
    Component.onCompleted: startCapture()
}

docs.title: Start and stop with a button
docs.text:
Cleave {
    id: cleave
}

Button {
    text: cleave.active ? "Stop" : "Start"
    onClicked: cleave.active ? cleave.stopCapture() : cleave.startCapture()
}

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
Scale the levels yourself

magnitudes are not clamped to 0..1. How big they get depends on the volume and the content, so apply your own gain and clamp, as the example does with * 5. Try a few values until your visual looks right.

Read magnitudes once per frame

magnitudes and peaks build a new list every time you read them. In a paint handler, copy the list once (const m = cleave.magnitudes) and index the copy, rather than writing cleave.magnitudes[i] inside a loop. If you use a Repeater, give it model: cleave.bandCount instead of binding it to magnitudes, which can rebuild every delegate on every update.

  • Repainting: call requestPaint() from onDataChanged, as the example does. Updates come at the analysis rate, up to about 47 per second.
  • startCapture() vs resumeCapture(): after an auto-suspend, use resumeCapture(). Calling startCapture() works too, but it does not emit suspendedChanged, so bindings on suspended would not update.
  • Changing source while running has no effect until the next startCapture().
  • Changing bandCount zeroes the levels, so it is best set once up front.
  • Silent frames are skipped: raise silenceThreshold if background hiss keeps your visual twitching.
  • Threading: audio is captured on the PipeWire thread and handed to the main thread, so all signals and properties are safe to use from QML.
  • Many bands cost more: every dataChanged re-evaluates anything bound to magnitudes, so keep bandCount reasonable.
  • Requirements: PipeWire (pipewire on Arch). The AUR packages pull it in for you.

docs.title: MaterialButtonGroup
docs.text:
A Material 3 expressive button group. A row of buttons that squish and spring when pressed, with optional single or multiple selection. It comes in two variants: spaced-out pills (Standard) and a tightly joined strip (Connected).

import Ryu.Extraa

MaterialButtonGroup {
    labels: ["Day", "Week", "Month"]
    selectionMode: MaterialButtonGroup.Single
    currentIndex: 0
    onToggled: (index, checked) => console.log(index, checked)
}

docs.title: Content
docs.text:
Property Type Default Description labels list<string> empty Text for each button. icons list<string> empty Icon glyph for each button. Needs iconFont. font font Font for the labels. Its pixel size is overridden by sizeStyle. iconFont font Font for the icon glyphs (Nerd Font or Material Symbols). fontWeight int 400 Label weight, 1 to 1000.

The number of buttons is the larger of labels.length and icons.length. A button can have a label, an icon, or both (icon first). Missing entries are just empty, so icons: ["a", "b"] with no labels gives you two icon-only buttons.

docs.title: Selection
docs.text: Property Type Default Description selectionMode SelectionMode NoSelection NoSelection, Single or Multiple. checkedIndices list<int> [] Indices of the checked buttons. Sorted, de-duplicated and clamped for you. currentIndex int -1 The first checked index, or -1 if nothing is checked. Setting it to a negative number clears the selection.

docs.title: Layout and appearance
docs.text: Property Type Default Description variant Variant Standard Standard or Connected. sizeStyle SizeStyle Small Preset height, padding, icon and font size (table below). spacing real -1 Gap between buttons. A negative value picks the M3 default for the variant and size. fillWidth bool false Stretch the buttons to fill the item's width, sharing the extra space equally. borderWidth real 0 Outline width on every button. springStiffness real 520 Spring stiffness. Higher is snappier. Minimum 1. springDamping real 0.5 Damping ratio, clamped to 0.05 to 2. Lower is bouncier.

docs.title: Colors
docs.text: Property Default Description color #E8DEF8 Background of unchecked buttons. checkedColor #6750A4 Background of checked buttons. textColor #1D192B Text and icon color of unchecked buttons. checkedTextColor #FFFFFF Text and icon color of checked buttons. borderColor #79747E Used with borderWidth.

docs.title: Enums
docs.text:
Variant: Standard, Connected

SelectionMode: NoSelection, Single, Multiple

SizeStyle: ExtraSmall, Small, Medium, Large, ExtraLarge

SizeStyle Height Side padding Icon size Font size Icon gap ExtraSmall 32 12 20 14 4 Small 40 16 24 14 8 Medium 56 24 24 16 8 Large 96 48 32 24 12 ExtraLarge 136 64 40 32 16

The default spacing for Standard is 18, 12, 8, 8 and 8 for the five sizes. For Connected it is always 2.

docs.title: Variants
docs.text:
• Standard: separate buttons. Unchecked buttons are full pills, and checked or pressed ones morph to rounded squares.
  • Connected: buttons sit 2 px apart as one strip. The outer ends are always fully round. The inner corners are small, and a checked or pressed button rounds off into a pill.

docs.title: Signals
docs.text: Signal Description clicked(int index) The user activated a button, with the mouse or keyboard. Fires in every selectionMode. toggled(int index, bool checked) The user changed the checked state of a button. Fires before clicked. checkedIndicesChanged() The selection changed from any source. currentIndex shares this signal.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text: Method Description isChecked(int index) Returns true if that button is checked. setChecked(int index, bool on) Checks or unchecks a button, following the rules of the current selectionMode.

docs.title: Segmented control (single choice)
docs.text:
MaterialButtonGroup {
    labels: ["Day", "Week", "Month"]
    selectionMode: MaterialButtonGroup.Single
    currentIndex: 1
    onToggled: (index, checked) => console.log("picked", index)
}

docs.title: Connected variant
docs.text:
MaterialButtonGroup {
    variant: MaterialButtonGroup.Connected
    sizeStyle: MaterialButtonGroup.Medium
    labels: ["Left", "Center", "Right"]
    selectionMode: MaterialButtonGroup.Single
    currentIndex: 0
}

docs.title: Multiple selection
docs.text:
MaterialButtonGroup {
    labels: ["Bold", "Italic", "Underline"]
    selectionMode: MaterialButtonGroup.Multiple
    checkedIndices: [0, 2]
    onToggled: (index, checked) => console.log(index, checked)
}

docs.title: Plain buttons (no selection)
docs.text:
With the default NoSelection, nothing stays checked and you just get clicked:

MaterialButtonGroup {
    labels: ["Cut", "Copy", "Paste"]
    onClicked: index => console.log("pressed", index)
}

docs.title: Icons and labels
docs.text:
MaterialButtonGroup {
    iconFont.family: "CaskaydiaCove NF"
    icons: ["", "", ""]   // use the glyphs from your font
    labels: ["Home", "Search", "Settings"]
    selectionMode: MaterialButtonGroup.Single
    currentIndex: 0
}

Leave labels out for icon-only buttons.

docs.title: Fill a container
docs.text:
MaterialButtonGroup {
    width: parent.width
    fillWidth: true
    labels: ["One", "Two", "Three"]
    selectionMode: MaterialButtonGroup.Single
}

docs.title: Custom colors and bounce
docs.text:
MaterialButtonGroup {
    labels: ["A", "B", "C"]
    selectionMode: MaterialButtonGroup.Single
    currentIndex: 0
    color: "#32362b"
    checkedColor: "#a0ec4c"
    textColor: "#e2e3d8"
    checkedTextColor: "#1b2b00"
    springStiffness: 700
    springDamping: 0.35
}

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
Declare labels and selectionMode before the selection

QML applies properties in the order you write them. checkedIndices and currentIndex throw away indices that don't exist yet, and are cleared outright while selectionMode is NoSelection. If you put currentIndex: 1 above labels, or above selectionMode: Single, the selection is silently dropped. Write the content and mode first, as the examples do.

Icons need iconFont

Icons are text glyphs, not images. Without an iconFont that contains them you get empty boxes.

  • Single selection is radio-like: clicking the already checked button does not uncheck it. It only emits clicked. Use Multiple if you need toggling off.
  • Programmatic changes are quiet: setting checkedIndices, currentIndex or calling setChecked() emits checkedIndicesChanged but not clicked or toggled. Use those two signals to react to the user only.
  • Switching mode trims the selection: moving to Single keeps only the first checked button, and moving to NoSelection clears it.
  • Signals are queued: toggled and clicked fire on the next event loop turn, not inside the mouse event.
  • Press squish: the pressed button grows by about 28% of the group's height and its neighbors shrink by the same amount, so the total width stays constant. It needs at least two buttons.
  • Size: the implicit width is the natural width of all buttons plus gaps, and the implicit height comes from sizeStyle. The buttons are centered vertically if you make the item taller.
  • No wrapping or clipping: if you set a width smaller than the natural width, the buttons simply run past the edge. fillWidth only ever grows them.
  • Mouse: a button activates when you release on the same one you pressed. Dragging off before release cancels it. The hit area of each button extends across the gap to its right.
  • Keyboard: the group takes focus on click or tab. Left and Right move the focus (no wrapping), and Space, Enter or Return activates the focused button. The focus highlight only shows after keyboard use.
  • Disabled: enabled: false dims the group to 38% opacity and ignores input.
  • Colors default to the M3 purple palette, so always bind them to your theme.

docs.title: MaterialList
docs.text:
A Material 3 list. Rows can have a leading icon, avatar or image, an overline, a headline, supporting text and trailing text or icon. It supports single and multiple selection, and comes in two variants: a flat Standard list and a Segmented expressive one where every row is its own rounded card.

import Ryu.Extraa

MaterialList {
    width: 360
    selectionMode: MaterialList.Single
    model: [
        { headline: "Inbox", supporting: "12 unread", leadingIcon: "\uf01c", trailingText: "12" },
        { headline: "Sent", leadingIcon: "\uf1d8" },
        "-",
        { overline: "Folder", headline: "Archive", supporting: "Everything old", leadingIcon: "\uf187" }
    ]
    iconFont.family: "CaskaydiaCove NF"
    onClicked: (index, item) => console.log(index, item.headline)
}

docs.title: Model
docs.text:
model is a list. Each entry is one of:

Entry Meaning "Text" A one-line item with that headline. "-" A divider. { ... } An item with the keys below. Key Type Description headline string Main text. supporting string Secondary text below the headline. overline string Small text above the headline. trailingText string Small text on the right edge. leadingIcon string Icon glyph on the left. Needs iconFont. trailingIcon string Icon glyph on the right. Needs iconFont. avatarText string Text (usually one letter) in a 40 px circle on the left. image string Image URL or path, shown as a 56 px rounded square on the left. enabled bool Default true. Disabled rows are dimmed and ignore input. divider bool Turns the entry into a divider.

If a row has several leading keys, image wins over avatarText, which wins over leadingIcon.

The row height follows the number of text lines: 56 for one line, 72 for two and 88 for three (overline, headline and supporting text all set).

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: Property Type Default Description model list empty The entries (see above). count int Read-only. Number of entries, dividers included. variant Variant Standard Standard or Segmented. selectionMode SelectionMode NoSelection NoSelection, Single or Multiple. checkedIndices list<int> [] Checked rows. Sorted, de-duplicated and clamped for you. currentIndex int -1 First checked index, or -1. font font Text font. Pixel sizes are fixed by the spec (16, 14 and 11). iconFont font Font for icon glyphs (Nerd Font or Material Symbols). springStiffness real 520 Spring stiffness. springDamping real 0.6 Damping ratio, clamped to 0.05 to 2.

docs.title: Colors
docs.text: Property Default Description itemColor transparent (Standard), #F3EDF7 (Segmented) Background of unchecked rows. selectedColor #E8DEF8 Background of checked rows. textColor #1D1B20 Headline color. Also the hover tint. selectedTextColor #1D192B Text and icon color of checked rows. supportingColor #49454F Overline, supporting and trailing text. iconColor supportingColor Icon color. avatarColor #EADDFF Avatar circle. avatarTextColor #21005D Avatar letter. dividerColor #CAC4D0 Divider line (Standard only).

docs.title: Enums
docs.text:
Variant: Standard, Segmented

SelectionMode: NoSelection, Single, Multiple

docs.title: Variants
docs.text:
• Standard: rows touch each other and have no corners. A "-" entry draws a 1 px divider inset by 16.
  • Segmented: rows sit 2 px apart. The first and last row of a group have round outer corners (16) and small inner ones (4). A pressed row springs to fully rounded. A "-" entry becomes an 8 px gap that splits the list into separate groups.

docs.title: Signals
docs.text: Signal Description clicked(int index, var item) The user activated a row. item is the original entry from model. Fires in every selectionMode. checkedIndicesChanged() The selection changed from any source. currentIndex shares this signal.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text: Method Description isChecked(int index) Returns true if that row is checked. setChecked(int index, bool on) Checks or unchecks a row, following the current selectionMode.

docs.title: Keyboard and mouse
docs.text: Input Action Up, Down Move the focus, skipping dividers and disabled rows. Wraps around. Home, End First or last row. Enter, Return, Space Activate the focused row. Hover Adds an 8% tint. Click A row activates when you release on the same one you pressed.

docs.title: Segmented, multiple selection
docs.text:
MaterialList {
    width: 360
    variant: MaterialList.Segmented
    selectionMode: MaterialList.Multiple
    model: ["Wi-Fi", "Bluetooth", "Airplane mode"]
    checkedIndices: [0]
}

docs.title: Avatars and trailing text
docs.text:
MaterialList {
    width: 360
    model: [
        { avatarText: "A", headline: "Ada", supporting: "Online", trailingText: "now" },
        { avatarText: "L", headline: "Linus", supporting: "Away", trailingText: "5 min" }
    ]
}

docs.title: Inside a scroll view
docs.text:
MaterialList is as tall as its rows and does not scroll. Put it in a Flickable for long lists:

Flickable {
    width: 360
    height: 400
    contentHeight: list.height
    clip: true

    MaterialList {
        id: list
        width: parent.width
        model: myItems
    }
}

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
Declare model and selectionMode before the selection

Like MaterialButtonGroup, indices that don't exist yet are dropped, and everything is cleared while selectionMode is NoSelection. Write model and selectionMode above checkedIndices or currentIndex.

Icons need iconFont

Icons are text glyphs, not images. Without an iconFont that contains them you get empty boxes.

  • Images are loaded once when model is set. Use absolute paths, ~/ paths, or file:// and qrc: URLs. For files next to your QML use Qt.resolvedUrl("x.png").toString().
  • Dividers are not selectable and are counted in indices.
  • Programmatic changes are quiet: setting checkedIndices or calling setChecked() emits checkedIndicesChanged but not clicked.
  • Single selection is radio-like: clicking the checked row keeps it checked.
  • Text is elided with … when it doesn't fit. There is no wrapping.
  • Changing model rebuilds the list and drops selected rows that no longer exist.
  • Disabled: enabled: false dims the list to 38% opacity and ignores input.
  • Colors default to the M3 purple palette, so always bind them to your theme.

docs.title: MaterialMenu
docs.text:
A Material 3 expressive context menu. A rounded popup with icons, shortcut hints, separators and a highlight that springs between rows. It opens from the point you click, flips away from screen edges, and supports keyboard navigation.

import Ryu.Extraa

MaterialMenu {
    id: menu
    model: [
        { label: "Refresh", icon: "\uf021", shortcut: "F5" },
        "-",
        { label: "Delete", icon: "\uf1f8", danger: true }
    ]
    onTriggered: (index, item) => console.log(index, item.label)
}

MouseArea {
    anchors.fill: parent
    acceptedButtons: Qt.RightButton
    onPressed: mouse => menu.popup(mouse.x, mouse.y)
}

docs.title: Model
docs.text:
model is a list. Each entry is one of:

Entry Meaning "Text" A plain item with that label. "-" A separator. { ... } An item with the keys below. Key Type Default Description label string empty Item text. icon string empty Icon glyph, drawn with iconFont. If any item has an icon, every row reserves the icon column. shortcut string empty Hint text aligned to the right edge. Display only. enabled bool true Disabled items are dimmed and cannot be selected. danger bool false Uses dangerColor for the row. separator bool false Turns the entry into a separator.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: Property Type Default Description model list empty The entries (see above). open bool false Whether the menu is shown. Prefer popup() to open it. currentIndex int -1 Read-only. The hovered or keyboard-selected row. closeOnTrigger bool true Close the menu when an item is activated. font font Label font. Its pixel size is overridden (14 px). fontWeight int 500 Label weight, 1 to 1000. iconFont font Font for icon glyphs (Nerd Font or Material Symbols). itemHeight real 40 Height of one row. Minimum 24. radius real 16 Corner radius of the menu. minimumWidth real 200 Minimum width. The menu grows to fit its content. edgeMargin real 8 Minimum distance kept from the parent's edges by popup(). borderWidth real 0 Outline width. springStiffness real 520 Spring stiffness. springDamping real 0.6 Damping ratio, clamped to 0.05 to 2.

docs.title: Colors
docs.text: Property Default Description color #F3EDF7 Menu background. textColor #1D1B20 Label color. Also the hover tint. iconColor textColor Icon color. shortcutColor #49454F Shortcut hint color. dangerColor #B3261E Text, icon and hover tint of danger items. separatorColor #CAC4D0 Separator line. borderColor #79747E Used with borderWidth.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text: Method Description popup(x, y) Opens the menu at a point in the parent's coordinates. Flips and clamps so it stays inside the parent. close() Closes the menu.

docs.title: Signals
docs.text: Signal Description triggered(int index, var item) An item was activated. item is the original entry from model. opened() The menu opened. closed() The menu closed (item chosen, Escape, or close()).

docs.title: Keyboard and mouse
docs.text: Input Action Up, Down Move the selection, skipping separators and disabled items. Wraps around. Home, End First or last item. Enter, Return, Space Activate the selected item. Escape Close. Hover Selects the row under the pointer. Click An item activates when you release on the same one you pressed.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
Dismiss on outside click yourself

A menu only receives input inside its own bounds. To close it when the user clicks elsewhere, call close() from a MouseArea behind it, as in the example above.

Put it in a full-size parent

popup() flips and clamps against the parent's size. Give the menu a parent that covers the area you want it to stay inside, such as the whole window or layer surface.

  • Opacity and scale are driven by the open animation. Don't set your own opacity or scale on the menu.
  • No submenus, scrolling or checkable items. A very long model simply makes a tall menu.
  • Changing model rebuilds the menu and resizes it to fit.
  • Icons are text glyphs, so they need an iconFont that contains them.
  • Disabled: enabled: false dims the menu to 38% opacity and ignores input.
  • Colors default to the M3 purple palette, so always bind them to your theme.

docs.title: MaterialSearchBox
docs.text:
A Material 3 expressive search bar. A pill-shaped, single-line text field with a leading icon, an optional trailing icon, and a clear button that springs in when there is text. It handles its own cursor, selection, clipboard and input method (IME) support.

import Ryu.Extraa

MaterialSearchBox {
    width: 320
    placeholderText: "Search"
    onTextChanged: console.log(text)
}

docs.title: Text
docs.text: Property Type Default Description text string empty The current text. Setting it from code moves the cursor to the end. placeholderText string empty Shown while text is empty. font font Font for the text and placeholder. Its pixel size is overridden and always drawn at 16 px. fontWeight int 400 Text weight, 1 to 1000. maxLength int 0 Maximum number of characters. 0 means unlimited. Longer text is truncated. readOnly bool false Blocks editing. Selecting and copying still work, and the cursor and clear button are hidden. cursorPosition int Read-only. Index of the cursor in text. hovered bool Read-only. True while the mouse is over the item.

docs.title: Icons
docs.text:
Property Type Default Description showSearchIcon bool true Shows the built-in magnifier on the left. leadingIconSource url empty Image for the leading icon. Replaces the magnifier. leadingIconText string empty Glyph for the leading icon. Needs iconFont. trailingIconSource url empty Image for a trailing icon on the right. trailingIconText string empty Glyph for the trailing icon. Needs iconFont. clearIconSource url empty Image to use instead of the built-in X on the clear button. iconFont font Font for leadingIconText and trailingIconText (Nerd Font or Material Symbols). clearable bool true Shows the clear button while there is text. Ignored when readOnly is true.

Icons are drawn at 24 px (the clear icon at 20 px). If both a source and a text glyph are set for the same slot, the source wins.

docs.title: Colors and border
docs.text: Property Default Description color #ECE6F0 Background of the bar. textColor #1D1B20 Text color. Also used for the hover tint. placeholderColor #49454F Placeholder color. iconColor #49454F Tint for every icon, the clear X, and the icon hover layer. borderColor #79747E Outline color while unfocused. borderWidth 0 Outline width. 0 means no outline. cursorColor #6750A4 Text cursor color. Also the outline color while focused. selectionColor rgba(103, 80, 164, 0.31) Selection highlight.

docs.title: Animation
docs.text: Property Type Default Description springStiffness real 520 Spring stiffness. Higher is snappier. Minimum 1. springDamping real 0.6 Damping ratio, clamped to 0.05 to 2. Lower is bouncier.

docs.title: Signals
docs.text:
Signal Description textChanged() text changed from any source. textEdited() The text was changed by the user: typing, pasting, deleting, cutting, IME input, or the clear button. Not emitted when you assign text from code. accepted() Enter or Return was pressed. cleared() The text was cleared with the clear button or by calling clear(). leadingClicked() The leading icon was clicked. trailingClicked() The trailing icon was clicked. cursorPositionChanged() The cursor moved. hoveredChanged() The mouse entered or left.

Every other property has the usual <property>Changed signal.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text: Method Description clear() Empties the text, moves the cursor to 0, and emits textChanged, textEdited and cleared. Does nothing if the text is already empty. selectAll() Selects the whole text.

docs.title: Animations
docs.text:
Three springs run inside the component:

Spring What it drives Visible as Hover An 8% tint of textColor over the bar A soft fade. Focus The outline color, from borderColor to cursorColor A color fade. Only visible when borderWidth > 0. Clear button The scale of the X and its hover circle A pop-in with overshoot up to 1.4x.

Only the clear button changes size, so it is the only spring where you can see a bounce. Lower springDamping (0.2 to 0.3) to make it more pronounced. The spring runs only while something is moving, so an idle search box costs nothing.

docs.title: Keyboard
docs.text:
Keys Action Left, Right Move the cursor. With a selection and no Shift, collapses to the start or end of it. Ctrl+Left, Ctrl+Right Move by word. Home, End Jump to the start or end. Shift + any movement Extend the selection. Backspace, Delete Delete one character, or the selection if there is one. Ctrl+Backspace Delete the word to the left of the cursor. Ctrl+Delete Delete the word to the right of the cursor. Ctrl+A Select all. Ctrl+C, Ctrl+X, Ctrl+V Copy, cut, paste. Line breaks in pasted text become spaces. Enter, Return Emit accepted().

The item takes focus on click or Tab.

docs.title: Mouse
docs.text:
• Click places the cursor. Shift+click extends the selection.
  • Drag inside the text selects.
  • Double click selects all the text (not a single word).
  • Icons and the clear button have a 40 px round hit area. They activate when you release on the same one you pressed. Dragging off cancels it.
  • The cursor is an I-beam over the text, a pointing hand over icons, and an arrow elsewhere.

docs.title: Basic
docs.text:
MaterialSearchBox {
    width: 320
    placeholderText: "Search"
    onAccepted: console.log("search for", text)
}

docs.title: Filtering a list
docs.text:
Column {
    spacing: 12

    MaterialSearchBox {
        id: search
        width: 320
        placeholderText: "Search fruits"
    }

    ListView {
        width: 320
        height: 240
        clip: true
        model: ["Apple", "Banana", "Cherry", "Mango"].filter(
            f => f.toLowerCase().includes(search.text.toLowerCase()))
        delegate: Text { text: modelData }
    }
}

docs.title: Custom icon
docs.text:
MaterialSearchBox {
    width: 320
    leadingIconSource: Qt.resolvedUrl("./search.svg")
    onLeadingClicked: console.log("leading clicked")
}

docs.title: Glyph icons
docs.text:
MaterialSearchBox {
    width: 320
    iconFont.family: "CaskaydiaCove NF"
    leadingIconText: "\ue8b6"
    trailingIconText: "\ue8b8"
    onTrailingClicked: console.log("settings")
}

Use the codepoints from your own font.

docs.title: Leading and trailing icons together
docs.text:
MaterialSearchBox {
    width: 360
    leadingIconSource: "search.svg"
    trailingIconSource: "mic.svg"
    onTrailingClicked: console.log("start voice search")
}

With a trailing icon, the clear button sits to its left.

docs.title: Outline that reacts to focus
docs.text:
MaterialSearchBox {
    width: 320
    borderWidth: 2
    borderColor: "#CAC4D0"
    cursorColor: "#6750A4"
}

The outline fades from borderColor to cursorColor when focused.

docs.title: Expand on focus
docs.text:
MaterialSearchBox {
    width: activeFocus ? 420 : 260

    Behavior on width {
        SpringAnimation { spring: 3.5; damping: 0.18; epsilon: 0.25 }
    }
}

The component does not resize itself, so the width bounce comes from a normal QML SpringAnimation.

docs.title: Bouncier clear button
docs.text:
MaterialSearchBox {
    width: 320
    springStiffness: 700
    springDamping: 0.25
}

docs.title: Limited and read-only
docs.text:
MaterialSearchBox {
    width: 240
    maxLength: 12
    placeholderText: "12 characters max"
}

MaterialSearchBox {
    width: 240
    readOnly: true
    text: "You can select me"
}

docs.title: Programmatic control
docs.text:
MaterialSearchBox {
    id: box
    width: 320
}

Row {
    Button { text: "Fill"; onClicked: box.text = "hello" }
    Button { text: "Select"; onClicked: box.selectAll() }
    Button { text: "Clear"; onClicked: box.clear() }
}

docs.title: Custom colors
docs.text:
MaterialSearchBox {
    width: 320
    color: "#32362b"
    textColor: "#e2e3d8"
    placeholderColor: "#a4a798"
    iconColor: "#a4a798"
    cursorColor: "#a0ec4c"
    selectionColor: "#40a0ec4c"
}

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
Icons are tinted

leadingIconSource, trailingIconSource and clearIconSource are drawn as a mask and filled with iconColor. A multicolor image becomes a single-color silhouette, so use simple monochrome icons.

SVG needs the Qt SVG plugin

Loading .svg files needs the Qt SVG image plugin (qt6-svg on Arch). Without it you get failed to load icon in the console even when the path is correct.

Glyph icons need iconFont

leadingIconText and trailingIconText are text glyphs. Without an iconFont that contains them you get empty boxes.

  • Image paths: *IconSource accepts file:// and qrc: URLs, absolute paths, ~/ paths, and paths relative to the QML file. If an icon does not show, check the console for could not resolve icon or failed to load icon.
  • Icon priority: for each slot, a source beats a text glyph, which beats the built-in icon. The leading slot shows if showSearchIcon, leadingIconText or leadingIconSource is set. Set showSearchIcon: false with no leading icon to remove it entirely.
  • Trailing and clear layout: the clear button moves left by 40 px when a trailing icon is present. The text area always keeps room for the clear button while clearable is true, even when it is hidden.
  • textEdited vs textChanged: use onTextEdited to react to the user only. Setting text from code emits textChanged but not textEdited, which avoids feedback loops. clear() counts as a user edit.
  • Setting text: the cursor moves to the end, any IME composition is dropped, and maxLength is applied.
  • Size: the bar is always 56 px tall with fully round ends. The implicit size is 360 x 56. If you make the item taller, the bar is centered vertically and clicks outside the bar are ignored.
  • Single line: the text scrolls horizontally to keep the cursor visible and is clipped to the text area. There is no wrapping.
  • Font size: font.pixelSize and font.pointSize are overridden. The text is always 16 px. Family, weight and style still apply.
  • IME: composition text is shown underlined and committed on confirmation, so CJK and other input methods work.
  • Disabled: enabled: false dims the item to 38% opacity and ignores all input.
  • Not a full TextInput: there is no undo/redo, context menu, validator, password mode, or Escape handling. Double click selects all, not one word.
  • Colors default to the M3 purple palette, so always bind them to your theme.

docs.title: MaterialSlider
docs.text:
A Material 3 expressive slider with a floating handle, segmented track and an optional value bubble. It works horizontally or vertically.

import Ryu.Extraa

MaterialSlider {
    width: 240
    value: 0.5
    onMoved: console.log(value)
}

docs.title: Value
docs.text: Property Type Default Description from real 0.0 Minimum value. to real 1.0 Maximum value. value real 0.0 Current value, clamped to from..to. stepSize real 0.0 Snap increment. 0 means continuous. pressed bool Read-only. True while dragging.

docs.title: Layout and appearance
docs.text: Property Type Default Description orientation Orientation Horizontal Horizontal or Vertical. sizeStyle SizeStyle ExtraSmall Preset track and handle sizes (table below). showStops bool true Dots along the track. Dots only appear for each step when stepSize > 0; otherwise just the end dot. showValueIndicator bool true Bubble with the value, shown while pressed. decimals int -1 Decimals in the bubble. -1 picks automatically from stepSize or the range. trackHeight real from style Overrides the preset. handleWidth real 4 Handle thickness. It narrows to half while pressed. handleHeight real from style Overrides the preset. handleGap real 6 Space between the handle and each track segment. outerRadius real trackHeight / 2 Corner radius of the track ends. innerRadius real 2 Corner radius next to the handle. stopSize real 4 Dot diameter. borderWidth real 0 Outline on the track segments.

docs.title: Icon
docs.text: Property Type Default Description iconText string empty Glyph drawn inside the active segment. Needs iconFont. iconFont font Font for iconText (Nerd Font or Material Symbols). iconSource url empty Image alternative. It is tinted with iconColor. iconColor color #FFFFFF Icon tint. iconSize real 24 Icon size in pixels.

docs.title: Colors
docs.text: Property Default Description color #6750A4 Active (filled) segment. trackColor #E8DEF8 Inactive segment and dots on the active side. handleColor #6750A4 The handle. borderColor transparent Used with borderWidth. indicatorColor #322F35 Value bubble background. indicatorTextColor #F5EFF7 Value bubble text.

docs.title: Enums
docs.text:
Orientation: Horizontal, Vertical

SizeStyle: ExtraSmall, Small, Medium, Large, ExtraLarge

SizeStyle Track height Handle height ExtraSmall 16 44 Small 24 44 Medium 40 52 Large 56 68 ExtraLarge 96 108

docs.title: Signals
docs.text: Signal Description moved() The user changed the value (mouse or keyboard). valueChanged() The value changed from any source. pressedChanged() Drag started or ended.

docs.title: Basic horizontal slider
docs.text:
MaterialSlider {
    width: 240
    value: 0.5
}

docs.title: Vertical slider
docs.text:
MaterialSlider {
    orientation: MaterialSlider.Vertical
    sizeStyle: MaterialSlider.Medium
    showValueIndicator: false
    value: 0.7

    Component.onCompleted: {
        width = 52
        height = 300
    }
}

docs.title: Stepped slider with a value bubble
docs.text:
MaterialSlider {
    width: 280
    from: 0
    to: 10
    stepSize: 1
    sizeStyle: MaterialSlider.Small
    value: 5
}

docs.title: Reacting to the user
docs.text:
Column {
    spacing: 12

    MaterialSlider {
        id: slider
        width: 240
        onMoved: label.text = "Value: " + value.toFixed(2)
    }

    Text {
        id: label
        text: "Value: 0.00"
    }
}

docs.title: Custom colors
docs.text:
MaterialSlider {
    width: 240
    value: 0.6
    color: "#a0ec4c"
    handleColor: "#a0ec4c"
    trackColor: "#32362b"
}

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
Set the size after the orientation

Changing orientation swaps width and height. If you bind a size and also set orientation: Vertical, the swap can fight your values. Setting width and height in Component.onCompleted, as the example does, avoids this.

Indicator takes space

With showValueIndicator: true, the item reserves 52 px on the cross axis for the bubble, which affects its implicit size. Turn it off when the slider sits in a tight layout.

  • Vertical direction: the value grows upward, so the bottom is from and the top is to.
  • moved vs valueChanged: use onMoved to react to the user only. Setting value from code emits valueChanged but not moved, which avoids feedback loops when writing back to a service.
  • Binding is kept: dragging does not break a value: ... binding, but any change of the bound source overwrites the dragged value. Pair the binding with onMoved to write back.
  • Programmatic value is clamped but not snapped to stepSize. Only user input snaps.
  • Keyboard: the slider takes focus on click or tab. Arrow keys step by stepSize, or by 1/20 of the range when continuous. Home and End jump to the ends.
  • Icon visibility: the icon only draws when trackHeight >= iconSize and the active segment is long enough to hold it.
  • Colors default to the M3 purple palette, so always bind them to your theme.

docs.title: WavyProgress
docs.text:
A progress indicator that can be a straight bar or a ring, with an optional animated wave. With amplitude: 0 it is a plain flat ring or bar.

import Ryu.Extraa

WavyProgress {
    width: 38
    height: 38
    style: WavyProgress.Circular
    indeterminate: false
    progress: 0.7
}

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: Property Type Default Description style Style Linear Linear or Circular. progress real 0.0 Value from 0 to 1. Clamped. Ignored while indeterminate is true. indeterminate bool true Plays a looping animation instead of showing progress. color color #6750A4 Color of the filled part. trackColor color #E8DEF8 Color of the unfilled part. amplitude real 3.0 Wave height in pixels. 0 gives a flat line. wavelength real 28.0 Distance between wave peaks in pixels. Minimum 4. waveSpeed real 0.8 Wave travel speed in cycles per second. 0 freezes the wave. strokeWidth real 4.0 Line thickness. Minimum 0.5. gap real 4.0 Space between the filled part and the track. Minimum 0.

docs.title: Enums
docs.text: Style: Linear, Circular

docs.title: Signals
docs.text: Only the automatic <property>Changed signals. There are no custom signals.

docs.title: Flat ring
docs.text:
WavyProgress {
    width: 48
    height: 48
    style: WavyProgress.Circular
    indeterminate: false
    progress: 0.7
    amplitude: 0
    waveSpeed: 0
    strokeWidth: 4
    gap: 0
    color: "#6750A4"
    trackColor: "#E8DEF8"
}

docs.title: Wavy bar
docs.text:
WavyProgress {
    width: 240
    height: 16
    style: WavyProgress.Linear
    indeterminate: false
    progress: 0.4
    amplitude: 3
    wavelength: 28
    waveSpeed: 0.8
}

docs.title: Loading spinner
docs.text:
WavyProgress {
    width: 48
    height: 48
    style: WavyProgress.Circular
}

docs.title: Animated progress
docs.text:
WavyProgress {
    id: bar
    width: 240
    height: 16
    indeterminate: false

    NumberAnimation on progress {
        from: 0
        to: 1
        duration: 4000
        loops: Animation.Infinite
    }
}

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
Static is free

The item only subscribes to window frames while something is moving: indeterminate is true, or amplitude > 0 and waveSpeed != 0. A flat ring with amplitude: 0 and waveSpeed: 0 costs nothing while idle.

Defaults animate

indeterminate defaults to true, so a bare WavyProgress {} spins forever. Set indeterminate: false to show progress.

  • Circular layout: the ring starts at 12 o'clock and fills clockwise. The radius is min(width, height) / 2 - strokeWidth / 2 - amplitude, so a larger amplitude shrinks the ring to keep the wave inside the item.
  • Circular waves: the number of waves around the ring is round(circumference / wavelength), so wavelength is approximate.
  • Linear amplitude is clamped so the wave never leaves the item's height.
  • Colors default to the M3 purple palette, so always bind them to your theme.

docs.title: MaterialShape
docs.text:
A filled shape from a set of 35 Material 3 Expressive shapes. Changing shape morphs the outline into the new one on a spring. It can also hold an image or a glyph, and it has a built-in loading mode that cycles through shapes.

import Ryu.Shapes

MaterialShape {
    width: 96
    height: 96
    shape: MaterialShape.Cookie9Sided
    color: "#6750A4"
}

docs.title: Shape and appearance
docs.text: Property Type Default Description shape Type Circle Which shape to draw. Changing it morphs to the new shape. color color #6750A4 Fill color. border.width real 0 Outline thickness. The shape is inset by half of it so the stroke stays inside the item. border.color color transparent Outline color. animated bool true When false, shape changes snap instead of morphing. morphing bool Read-only. True while a morph is running. springStiffness real 420 Morph spring stiffness. Minimum 1. springDamping real 0.6 Morph damping ratio, clamped to 0.05..2. Lower values bounce more.

docs.title: Loading
docs.text:
Property Type Default Description loading bool false Cycles through shapes forever, rotating a step each time. loadingGap int 120 Pause in ms between a morph finishing and the next one starting. loadingKick real 90 Degrees added to the rotation target on every step. Can be negative. loadingAllShapes bool false Cycle through all 35 shapes in enum order. loadingSequence list<int> empty Custom order, using MaterialShape.<Shape> values.

If none of the sequence options are set, the loop uses a curated 7-shape order: SoftBurst, Cookie9Sided, Pentagon, Pill, Sunny, Cookie4Sided, Oval.

docs.title: Contained

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
Always set a size

MaterialShape has no implicit size. Without width and height (or a layout that provides them) it draws nothing, or fills whatever the parent gives it.

Shapes fill 90% of the item

The outline is drawn at 90% of the smaller side, leaving room for the spring overshoot during a morph. Keep that in mind when aligning it with other items.

  • Contained size: in contained mode the shape's extent is 0.9 × containedScale of the circle. For a tight fit try 0.8 to 0.9. Near 1.0, spiky shapes like Sunny and Burst can touch the edge while they rotate.
  • Loading rotation: the item rotates itself with rotation. A glyph or image is counter-rotated so it stays upright. Don't set your own rotation while loading is true.
  • Loading priority: loadingAllShapes wins over loadingSequence, which wins over the default loop. Invalid numbers in loadingSequence are dropped, and an empty or fully invalid list falls back to the default.
  • Hidden items cost nothing: if the item is hidden or removed from its window, a running morph finishes immediately and the loading timer stops. It resumes when the item is visible again.
  • No animation when hidden: setting shape on an invisible item, or before the component is complete, snaps instead of morphing.
  • First morph cost: each pair of shapes is aligned the first time it is used and cached, so the first lap of loadingAllShapes can hitch slightly on the detailed shapes (Boom, SoftBoom).
  • Image paths: source accepts file:// and qrc: URLs, absolute paths, ~/ paths, and paths relative to the QML file.
  • Contained border: when contained is true, the border outlines the circle, not the shape.
  • Colors default to the M3 purple palette, so always bind them to your theme.
